articles.title: Alonso: "¿2027? Esta situación es la que es..."
articles.standfirst: El asturiano apenas pasó de 20 vueltas en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, mostró su frustración y mantiene esperanza en la mejora de Honda en el futuro
articles.summary: El asturiano apenas pasó de 20 vueltas en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, mostró su frustración y mantiene esperanza en la mejora de Honda en el futuro
articles.body: Fernando Alonso no cruzó la vuelta 22 del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán cuando tuvo que verse obligado a abandonar. También lo hizo un rato antes su compañero en Aston Martin, Lance Stroll. En el seno del equipo británico ya sabían que la cita caucásica no iba a ser más que una prueba de un coche aligerado y con algún retoque, pero los más de dos kilómetros de recta que atraviesan el Boulevard de Bakú también sacaron a la luz las debilidades del proyecto. Las principales son de Honda, el suministrador de motores. No existe más que una confirmación de unos problemas que no se solucionan y que dejan una papeleta difícil de cara al 2027. Tanto de un proyecto que tiene todo para pasar al frente como de su estrella, Fernando Alonso. No ha tomado una decisión y sabe lo que hay. "Es lo que es esta situación. Sabemos que hay cosas que se escapan de nuestro control y trabajamos para resolver los problemas", precisó el asturiano ante la prensa internacional. El de Oviedo mantiene la fe dentro de lo que cabe. "La falta de rendimiento es una cosa, pero sabemos lo que todo el mundo intenta mejorar. No ayudan, claro, los problemas de fiabilidad de cada semana si no tienes el kilometraje. Creo que estamos haciendo nuestra parte del trabajo, que consiste en ayudar al equipo a intentar entender cómo ganar velocidad en las curvas", explicó. Con mensaje a Honda. "Cuando pisamos el acelerador y estamos en la recta, tenemos que confiar en Honda y en que vaya mejorando cada vez más. Hemos dado un paso adelante con la mejora del motor. Pero no es suficiente y tenemos que seguir trabajando", agregó. En Bakú eso no ocurrió. Durante la carrera repitió que sufría problemas con el motor y terminó abandonando pese a que el equipo no detectaba lo mismo desde el muro. "No vi ninguna alarma. Todo funcionaba bien, pero empecé a perder mucho en la recta. Como 1,5 segundos. Era algo anómalo", recordó. Lo mejor es que llegan circuitos teóricamente favorables. "Si hay menos recta, mejor para nosotros. Pero sigues necesitando potencia", expresó sobre lo que vendrá en Malasia y Singapur. Con cautela hasta para el circuito urbano que llegará en 15 días. "Hasta allí lo necesitas. Budapest depende menos de la potencia que Singapur. Aunque la situación será mejor que en Monza y Bakú. Además, tenemos que hacerlo mejor como equipo", cerró.

articles.title: Así queda el Mundial de F1 tras el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán en Bakú
articles.standfirst: Antonelli hace una carrera de campeón
articles.summary: Antonelli hace una carrera de campeón
articles.body: Final del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, y ya van 15. Un fin de semana en el que George Russell demostró una superioridad ante el resto y en el que aprovechó los errores de su compañero de equipo y líder del Mundial, recortándole 15 puntos. El británico suma así su tercera victoria de la temporada y mantiene viva la lucha por el Mundial, con un total de 261 puntos, a 63 puntos de su compañero, Kimi Antonelli. Max Verstappen acabó 2º, a una décima del de Mercedes y tras una intensa lucha que se llevó hasta línea de meta. Tras un fin de semana dando pasos adelante y mostrando ser el único capaz de 'ponerle los puntos sobre las íes' a Russell, el neerlandés tuvo problemas durante la Qualy, clasificando finalmente 8º. Aún y así, cambió todos los componentes de combustión, aunque sin penalización por tener recambios, y pudo ir adelantando posiciones hasta colocarse 3º, justo por detrás de Oscar Piastri, quien acabó cometiendo un error y regalándole la 2ª plaza a Verstappen. El último escalón del Pódium fue para Isack Hadjar, quien regresaba tras una dura lesión que le mantuvo fuera de combate tres Grandes Premios. Aún y así, el francés pudo ir dando pasos adelante durante todo el fin de semana y, tras clasificar 4º en parrilla y mantener una lucha con su compañero de equipo, Verstappen, el de Red Bull Racing acabó 3º en Bakú. Un error en la Q1 condenó a Kimi Antonelli a partir 16º en la carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. Aún y así, el italiano mantuvo la calma y, a pesar de perder posiciones en la salida, confió en su talento y en su monoplaza, aprovechándose de los infortunios de otros pilotos por delante de él y firmar un 5º puesto. Aunque no sea la remontada que le hubiera gustado y la que todo el mundo esperaba, Antonelli suma 12 puntos que le pueden dar el Mundial. Los problemas se le acumulan a Aston Martin y, en especial, a Honda, acabando con la paciencia del piloto español. El Bicampeón del Mundo tan solo completó 21 vueltas muy frustrantes y en las que se le vio claramente enfadado, ante la incapacidad hacerle frente a los rivales con su monoplaza. Además, a esto se le añade el desastre que ha supuesto el fin de semana en general. Partía con una sanción de 25 posiciones por cambiar su Unidad de Potencia, la cual se acabó rompiendo, haciendo que tuvieran que volver a montar el motor antiguo. Problemas que se suman y que van calando en el piloto español, cuya amenaza de acabar su historia con la Fórmula 1 cada vez se hace más latente. Con mejoras en su Williams, aunque tampoco como para lanzar cohetes, Carlos ha podido sacarle provecho y, tras meterse en Q3 y clasificar 9º, el madrileño tuvo que volver a tirar de talento para salvar un punto. Una sanción por bandera amarilla condenó a Sainz a salir desde la 14ª posición, la cuál acabó siendo un desastre. Perdió varias posiciones en la salida y no tuvo más remedio que remontar, aprovechándose, eso sí, de los diversos incidentes que se formaron por delante. Finalmente pudo pasar a Hulkenberg a menos de 5 vueltas para el final, firmando así un 10º puesto. Parecía que este iba a ser un Mundial a 4 entre los dos Mercedes y los dos Ferrari. Sin embargo, poco a poco los de la escudería italiana han ido diluyéndose de la batalla y, Lewis Hamilton, quien podría haber mantenido un poco más de tiempo la batalla viva, carrera tras carrera termina con sus opciones al que sería su 8º Título de F1, terminando, esta vez, 6º, por detrás de Kimi Antonelli.

articles.title: Sun Goddess passes 'massive test' to rule supreme in Cheveley Park
articles.summary: Aidan O'Brien's star filly Sun Goddess recorded a third Group One success with an emphatic display in the Cheveley Park Stakes, in a record-setting time.
articles.body:
Sun Goddess and fellow Group One heroine Senorita Bonita travelled in tandem in midfield as Snowing and Moonrise set a strong pace up the six furlongs of the Rowley Mile.

Senorita Bonita was the first to show her hand, with the smooth-travelling Libertango launching her attack under Billy Loughnane on the far side from the back of the field.

But Sun Goddess found plenty for Ryan Moore on meeting the rising ground, with the 5-6 favourite engaging top gear to win by a going-away length from Libertango, making it her third top-level win of the campaign. Senorita Bonita was only able to finish fifth after not getting home.

O'Brien, who saddled this year's 1000 Guineas heroine True Love to win this race 12 months ago, said: "That is a massive run after winning over seven furlongs (Moyglare Stud Stakes) on soft ground, it was some change today. It was a massive test and she's passed it.

"She looks a freak doesn't she to be doing what she is doing and you have to remember she's a two-year-old filly racing at the top level every day. It's incredible and I can't remember having one that classy, with that speed and distance range before, she looks really unusual.

"She's unique and to have the mental capacity and physical (attributes) to match it. She's come back there and she's in no way stressed at all.

"She came off the bridle early which meant she would get into her tempo as we were worried she would travel and then come off the bridle and find everything happening too quickly. But once she came off it early she was always going to be really hard to handle.

"She's big and doesn't look like a two-year-old, she's more like a three-year-old and a massive big specimen. Even if she didn't change any from now until next year she would be plenty big and would still be considered a big three-year-old. It's very unusual."

He went on: "The lads got her in Doncaster and it was great she was able to go back and win that (sales) race at York earlier in the summer, it's a great initiative and a very big pot."

Sun Goddess was made 6-4 favourite for next year's 1000 Guineas by BOYLE Sports, but before that she could board the plane to Keeneland for the Breeders' Cup to test her mettle over a mile.

O'Brien added: "We'll see how she is and the next week or so will tell us how she is and whether this has taken much out of her.

"She is not blowing very hard and when we were tacking up there was no anxiety. She's as cool as a cucumber and Ryan was over the moon with her."

articles.title: Orthodox leaves Prix Morny defeat behind in Middle Park
articles.summary: The Clive Cox-trained Norfolk hero Orthodox bounced back from his Prix Morny defeat with a gutsy display to see off Force Noir in a thrilling finish to the Middle Park at Newmarket.
articles.body:
Force Noir cut out the early running as he set a sharp pace at the head of field, but Rossa Ryan put down his challenge early and asked Norfolk Stakes winner Orthodox for an effort at the three-furlong marker.

The Clive Cox-trained 7-2 chance was pushed all the way to the line by Robson De Aguiar's Force Noir at a big price and just prevailed by a neck, with favourite Inner City Blues never getting into it.

It was a welcome return to winning ways for the Royal Ascot scorer and Cox said: "We always had confidence in him and it was always a question of would he handle the track with the quicker ground a bonus for this time of year.

"Sometimes it is not as quick as this and I'm just thrilled he has shown what we all see at home, as he is pretty special in the mornings and he's special in the afternoons as well. He's tough and very able and it was a big team effort to get him here and I'm over the moon.

"I think he got away with the track and Rossa was supreme the way he coaxed him through the dip and then set sail after that. I thought it was a supreme ride and I'm thrilled. Rossa is a regular in the mornings and knows exactly what he's riding and what he's up against as well."

It was the third time Cox has scooped the Middle Park after Reckless Abandon (2012) and Supremacy (2020) who like Orthodox was owned by Jason Goddard.

With his future clearly lying in the sprint division in which Cox regularly thrives, Orthodox was handed a quote of 12-1 by Ladbrokes and Coral for next year's Commonwealth Cup at the Royal meeting.

However, before that a trip to America for the Breeders' Cup will be discussed by connections.

Cox continued: "I would be hugely excited by this fellow. I know his family really well and his aunt won the Queen Mary for us (Heartache).

"I think he's blessed with the ability to race over five furlongs or six, but I don't think there can be any doubt he gets six and he proved that today.

"He had the gears to win well over five furlongs at Ascot and he's a very talented sprinter and a joy to have.

"It's a joy to have these horses and it means the world. He could go to the Breeders' Cup and we'll see how he comes back and discuss it with Jason. It is a possibility, but we have to enjoy today first and then discuss the future over the next few days."

Haffner records straightforward Royal Lodge success

Haffner left a disappointing performance in the National Stakes firmly behind him with a clear-cut victory in the Tattersalls Online Royal Lodge Stakes at Newmarket.

The Charlie Appleby-trained pair of Quest For Stars and First Law disputed the early lead with the latter racing keenly on the far side of the course in isolation with Iwasjustsaying.

The Aidan O'Brien-trained Haffner was the first to lay down his challenge a furlong and a half out and pulled clear of the field with First Law and Quest For Stars unable to go with him.

The well-backed 7-4 favourite went on to oblige by one and a quarter lengths to give O'Brien a record eighth Royal Lodge and Ryan Moore his first. Karl Burke's Burning Up stayed on best of the rest for second in the colours of last year's winner, Bow Echo.

O'Brien said: "The ground got soft at the Curragh the last day which didn't suit him. He's going to be a lovely middle-distance horse next year, he's going to be a French Derby type horse. He'll get the Guineas trip on his ear, will stay a mile and a quarter and could even get further, so I'm delighted.

"He's a good mover and we didn't think the ground was going to be as soft as it was at the Curragh. He's a beautiful mover and we were happy to draw a line through that and he was always in control today. Ryan gave him a beautiful uncomplicated ride and it was very simple really.

"His form was different class really and his only blip was in the National Stakes. We knew that was because of the ground and we knew he would get the mile very easily. He's an Acomb winner and his form is so strong."

Paddy Power make Haffner a 4-1 chance for the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf at Keeneland next month and O'Brien indicated that could be the next destination for the talented son of Justify.

O'Brien added: "America is very possible next, where he will get nice ground. He would love the Breeders' Cup round a bend and the mile would be very easy for him, so we'll see what the lads want to do.

"America was always a possibility and the last day was a blip, but we had to come here today to make sure we knew exactly that it was and he's got back on track.

"I think he could start in a Guineas next year and then we will see him stepping up in trip."

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for Franco Colapinto race ban after Azerbaijan GP three-car collision with Alpines
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto apologetic for the "big mistake" that saw him cause chain reaction collision with team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris, forcing all three to retire; Colapinto to serve grid drop at Bahrain GP; Norris says "just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1"
articles.body:
At the first Safety Car restart on lap 36, Colapinto badly misjudged his braking into the first corner and, carrying too much speed, steamed into the side of Alpine team-mate Gasly, whose car was sent into Norris' McLaren on its outside.

Norris was spun into the barriers, with the two Alpines also forced to retire with damage. Gasly had been running seventh, Norris eighth and Colapinto 10th.

A frustrated Norris said: "At the end of the day, I just got taken out.

"Just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1, to be honest."

Speaking to the written media, the reigning world champion added: "I've not seen it, but if you cause a crash in a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban.

"I just got taken out. And the FIA should be stricter by starting to hand out bans for this kind of stuff."

Colapinto was apologetic on both team radio and then in his interviews afterwards for what he admitted was a "big mistake".

"Just to all the team, not only to Pierre, but it's just a big mistake," said Colapinto.

"So a big, big sorry to Pierre, to everyone in the factory that has been working really hard. We were with both cars in the points so very sad and disappointed.

"Big, big sorry, it's a big mistake. Just cold brakes, cold tyres and locked up and completely out of control.

"Unfortunately, I also took Pierre out and Lando of course but big sorry to both of them."

Colapinto was handed a 10-second time penalty by stewards for causing the collision but, as he had already retired from the race and so could not serve it, the sanction was converted into a five-place grid penalty for this coming week's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

F1 has a totting-up procedure in place for indiscretions on track, with drivers banned for a race if they accrue 12 penalty points on their superlicence over a rolling 12-month period. Colapinto, who is currently on four points, did not have any penalty points applied to his licence for Saturday's incident in addition to the in-lieu Bahrain grid drop.

'You want to be against the best drivers - Norris unimpressed with Colapinto error

Norris described Colapinto's driving as "just careless" and unbecoming of F1.

"It costs a lot of money, all my parts are in the bin now," he added.

"It is not driving that deserves to be in Formula 1

"In Formula 1 you would expect that drivers can anticipate that the grip will be low and tyre temperatures are low.

"You want to be against the best drivers and when stuff like this happens it is because, yeah, they shouldn't be there."

Norris said he had already been enduring an "impossible race" owing to straight-line speed issues with his car. He had dropped behind Gasly six laps earlier by running wide at the first turn.

I'm still struggling to process the outcome - Gasly's reaction to costly Alpine result

Gasly had been on course to equal his second-best result of the season with seventh place amid a strong weekend on the street track for the Frenchman.

With Colapinto also having been running in the points at the time of the Safety Car, Alpine were on course to almost wipe out their pre-race deficit of nine points to rivals Racing Bulls - who at that stage ran 12th and 14th - in the chase for fifth place in the Constructors' Championship.

However, they leave the race 15 points behind Racing Bulls after a late-race surge saw Arvid Lindblad take seventh place instead.

Admitting he was almost lost for words, Gasly told Sky Sports F1 : "It's not easy.

"We did a very good weekend and it was one of the best race cars we've had this season and the pace was great, keeping up with Lewis [Hamilton] and Lando for most of the race and we had a 14 or 15-second gap to the midfield.

"So I think a lot of positives to take away but I'm still struggling to process the outcome and the fact we had both cars in the points and in the end we got outscored by Racing Bulls by a lot of points.

"Not an ideal day but I'm sure we are going to move on from it. Unfortunately, we have lost out today, hopefully we can make it up to the end of the year."

Gasly spoke on Wednesday about the "completely inappropriate" social media abuse that he and family members had received in the wake of an incident on track with Colapinto at the previous race in Madrid. Colapinto and Alpine have consistently condemned abuse aimed at other drivers from some Argentine fans online.

Colapinto and Gasly are both already confirmed at the team for next season.

Asked if he was confident his partnership with Colapinto could continue to work, Gasly replied: "Respect. It's all about respect. As long as there is respect, everything is possible."

Colapinto added: "We are good. We have always been quite good together. Since we worked together for the first time, we got on very well so we need to move on."

articles.title: Pierre Royal strikes Cambridgeshire gold for Ireland
articles.summary: A first trip to Newmarket was a winning one for Adrian McGuinness as the only Irish raider Pierre Royal struck gold in the coveted Cambridgeshire Handicap.
articles.body:
But connections of the Adrian McGuinness-trained four-year-old had a tense wait before the judge confirmed he had edged Crest Of Fire to become the first Irish-trained winner of the race this century.

Both the winner and second came from the group on the far side and it was Jack Channon's Crest Of Fire who was first to emerge in the hands of Tom Marquand.

But he was stalked all the way by the Mikey Sheehy-ridden Pierre Royal and the 33-1 shot reeled him to just get up.

Altareq ran a huge race for Jim Goldie and Lauren Young to claim third at 100-1 with favourite Gavriel the best of the near-side runners in fourth.

McGuinness said: "I wasn't surprised as we have been running him on soft ground and it's been killing me. He was third in an Irish Cambridgeshire on soft ground and I said I'd come here for the better ground. We gave it some cheer and I've just dashed back from the winning post.

"We only made our minds up to come last Monday and he ran very well in the Irish Cambridgeshire and then we ran him back over one-mile-two and it was soft and he didn't handle it.

"He's a lovely horse to train and he's very easy on himself, he travels over well and he eats and like myself can get a bit big sometimes. He just eats, sleeps and drinks.

"There's a great bunch of lads involved in this horse and they've had a great time with him. He's paid his way plenty and cost only 48,000 guineas at Newmarket last year."

He went on: "I told Mikey to sit out the back as he had plenty of boot and in all fairness to Mikey I think one of his last rides for me he took was a spare on a reserve that won the Galway Mile and he's a top-class rider.

"I'm delighted I got him and only rang his agent a couple of days ago to see if he was available as I wanted to pick someone who is lucky for me. He's top notch."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli: F1 championship leader says he was 'driving like his grandma' due to lack of confidence at Azerbaijan GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli's world champions lead over George Russell was reduced to 66 points following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix; Antonelli recovered from 16th on the grid to finish fifth, while Russel won from pole position
articles.body:
Antonelli staged a decent recovery in Saturday's race to come from 16th on the grid, following a crash in qualifying, to finish fifth, but his championship lead over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell was reduced to 66 points as the Brit claimed victory.

The 20-year-old Italian has shown remarkable consistency to build a commanding lead at the top of the standings, but struggled in Baku after missing a significant chunk of practice due to technical issues with his car.

"I was driving a bit like my grandmother today, just damage save mode," Antonelli said. "I didn't take risks. Before making a move, I was making sure that I could go for it."

Expectations were high given Antonelli had remarkably come from 19th on the grid to win his home race at Monza earlier in September, but his progress was far more steady this time around.

"If I had the same pace as at Monza or in previous races, it would have been different," Antonelli said.

"It would have been like just full attack. But today, I realised very early that first of all, it was a lot harder to overtake with a train of cars all in Overtake Mode, then I didn't have the same pace as I had previously, so the mindset changed very quickly."

Antonelli actually dropped a place at the start, and it took him 17 laps to work his way up into the top 10.

He then benefitted from errors made by drivers ahead as he made further progress. He also survived a near-miss at the first of two rolling restarts following Safety Cars as he avoided a crash that took three cars out of the race, and was able to continue despite contact with the Haas of Oliver Bearman.

Antonelli said: "After the restart, I had big floor damage. My whole left side was gone with the contact.

"After that, the car was very sketchy to drive, and I still tried to get to P4, but all in all, it's one of those days where you have to be happy with P5.

"Also seeing so many people doing mistakes, you kind of pull back a little bit because I just took advantage of everyone else's mistakes and just move forward."

Antonelli doesn't have to wait long to return to the track with the second of a triple-header of races coming next weekend with the Bahrain Grand Prix, which is being hosted by Malaysia amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Russell produced his most complete weekend since the opening round of the season in Australia, taking a victory that would have been dominant without the Safety Car interruptions.

Antonelli remains a heavy favourite for the title, especially given Russell must take a grid penalty for changing his engine between now and the end of the season.

It was therefore unsurprising that the championship leader was retaining a positive outlook ahead of the next race.

"It's exciting," Antonelli told Sky Sports F1 . "George has done an incredible weekend, he's driven incredibly. He had a lot of confidence.

"And this weekend was my worst of the year by far in terms of performance. I wasn't there, I wasn't really present, especially with what happened so early on."
